digest:
The day’s papers weave a rich tapestry around holography and conformal dynamics.  In the holographic direction, the authors of *Holographic entropy inequalities & typical states* revisit the linear entropy bounds derived from the Ryu–Takayanagi prescription, probing their persistence beyond static AdS geometries and into classical Einstein gravity and non‑holographic settings.  Complementing this, *All‑plus Yang–Mills and gravity wavefunctions in de Sitter space* delivers compact, self‑dual sewing formulas for higher‑point wavefunctions in dS(_4), revealing a non‑crossing polygonal structure for Yang–Mills and an alternating‑tree plus Chern–Simons term for gravity—tools that sharpen our understanding of dS holography and boundary data.  The new family of higher‑spin theories in *Nonlinear Higher‑Spin Theory in (O(4,1)) de Sitter Space* introduces fermionic sectors and a (mathbb{Z}_2	imesmathbb{Z}_2) superalgebra, hinting at novel dS duals with time‑reversal or spacetime‑doubling features.  Meanwhile, *Theory and Cosmology of Biverse Volume‑Normalized Gravity* proposes a 5D bulk embedding that tames loop divergences, yields a ghost‑free massive graviton, and predicts a vanishing tensor‑to‑scalar ratio—an intriguing holographic route to the cosmological constant problem.

On the conformal side, the universal thermal‑entropy bound in *The Free Scalar as a Thermal Envelope for Three‑Dimensional CFTs* links entropy density to the stress‑tensor two‑point coefficient, saturating for the free scalar and tying into conformal‑collider positivity.  The memory‑effect study *On memory effects in odd spacetime dimensions* uncovers a universal electromagnetic memory tied to the leading soft photon theorem, offering a new angle for celestial amplitude investigations.  *One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres–Douglas* constructs affine schemes that encode Higgs branches and Macdonald indices, suggesting deep ties to W‑algebras and the geometric Langlands program.  In a complementary algebraic direction, *Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity* extends Miyamoto’s theorem to weight‑2 vectors, producing quasi‑modular forms that could inform modular bootstrap of conformal blocks.  Together, these works advance higher‑point structures, celestial memory, and the algebraic underpinnings of holographic and conformal field theories, resonating strongly with the physicist’s interests in holography, celestial amplitudes, Langlands‑type correspondences, and higher‑point Witten‑diagram‑like structures.

papers.title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
papers.authors: Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song
papers.abstract: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.
papers.summary: This paper constructs affine schemes whose Jacobian rings encode the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of Argyres–Douglas theories, using syzygy‑maximizing potentials derived from Coxeter orbit spaces. It proposes a deep link between these geometric structures and Zhu’s C₂‑algebras of affine VOAs, hinting at connections to W‑algebras and the geometric Langlands program.

papers.title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index
papers.abstract: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.
papers.summary: This work constructs thousands of holomorphic N=1 superconformal field theories with minimal Witten index, using ternary codes and AI-assisted searches to achieve central charges c=12k and index 24/gcd(24,k). It also connects these VOAs to Landau–Ginzburg orbifolds and establishes new results on ternary code indices, with implications for the 576‑periodicity of TMF via the Segal–Stolz–Teichner conjecture.

papers.title: The Free Scalar as a Thermal Envelope for Three-Dimensional CFTs
papers.abstract: We conjecture that every unitary three-dimensional conformal field theory obeys $c_S/C_T\leq16\pi\zeta(3)$, where $s=c_ST^2$ is the thermal entropy density and $C_T$ the stress-tensor two-point coefficient, with equality for free scalars. We embed this in a stronger conjecture: on $S^1\times H^2$, the $C_T$-normalized hyperbolic heat capacity is bounded above by that of the free scalar for all $T\geq(2\pi R)^{-1}$. Near the conformal temperature, for theories smooth from the high-temperature side and without boundary terms in the modular Hamiltonian, the heat-capacity bound follows from conformal-collider positivity. We test the conjectures in free, interacting large-$N$, and holographic theories. Monte Carlo data for the three-dimensional Ising and $O(N)$ models also obey the flat-space bound.
papers.summary: The authors propose a universal bound on the ratio of thermal entropy density to the stress‑tensor two‑point coefficient in any unitary 3D CFT, saturated by the free scalar. They verify the bound in free, large‑N, holographic models and Monte‑Carlo data, linking it to conformal‑collider positivity and hyperbolic heat capacity.

papers.title: Spin-Induced Coordinate Noncommutativity of the Covariant Centroid
papers.authors: Daniel Guimaraes Tedesco, Luiz Paulo Colatto
papers.abstract:
The Tulczyjew-Dixon centroid of a massive spinning particle, built as a composite of canonical Poincar'e variables, carries the exact coordinate algebra $\{X^\mu,X^
u\}=-S^{\mu
u}/p^2$, whose noncommutativity bivector is the transverse spin tensor of the particle itself rather than an external background. That bracket and its Compton-scale magnitude are already known, and we recover them here as the starting point of the analysis, not as a result. What the composite realization settles is the domain on which the algebra may be used. Closure of the Jacobi identity requires $p^{-2}$ to remain operator valued, and the exactness domain is the convex timelike interior $\Omega_\mu$, on which states supported on a single mass shell are distributional. We show that freezing $p^2$ to its shell value inside the centroid leaves every two-operator commutator unchanged on shell, so that the projected position dictionary, the Berry cancellation and the endpoint transversality identity are untouched, while the same substitution fails from three insertions onward, with residue the truncated Jacobiator $2\epsilon^{\mu
uho\sigma}W_\sigma/(p^2)^2$. This two-versus-three criterion replaces the qualitative restriction to shell-preserving matrix elements and states which constructions built on a fixed-shell bivector $\Theta_m$ remain valid. We then follow the algebra through positive-energy projection, packet-conditioned Moyal fibers, Compton routing holonomy and projected nonassociative products, recording for each layer whether it falls on the safe side of the criterion. No prediction beyond QED follows. In the geometric branch the physical amplitude reduces to the QED amplitude, and the transverse matching coefficients remain uncomputed.
papers.summary: The paper revisits the exact coordinate algebra of the Tulczyjew-Dixon centroid for a massive spinning particle, showing that the noncommutativity bivector is the particle’s transverse spin tensor and that the Jacobi identity imposes a domain constraint on the operator‑valued mass‑shell factor. It then analyzes the impact of freezing the mass‑shell condition on various operator products, concluding that the resulting nonassociative structures do not lead to new predictions beyond standard QED.

papers.title: Berends-Giele currents for higher derivative gauge theories
papers.abstract: We derive Berends-Giele (BG) currents for higher derivative scalar QED (HDQED) and Yang-Mills (HDYM). In HDQED, we first compute the propagators and the vertices from the higher derivative Lagrangian and discuss the pole structures of the photon and the scalar. We then compute the BG currents using the Feynman diagram setup and prove the Ward identities for these currents at two and three points. Next, we used the perturbiner formalism to re-compute these currents and show that they are consistent with the Feynman diagram approach. In a similar fashion, we derive the BG currents in higher derivative Yang-Mills and find that remarkably, these currents are equal to pure Yang-Mills currents when all external on-shell legs are massless gluons. We prove this in all generality using the BG recursion and explicitly show this at lower points. However, the genuine higher derivative structure enters when one or many on-shell states are the so called massive Merlin modes. Using the multi-particle currents, we reproduce the result that all tree level amplitudes with one Merlin particle vanishes and the three and four Merlin amplitudes match the previously computed result. The future prospects of BG recursion for higher derivative gravity and off-shell colour- kinematics duality is also discussed.
papers.summary: This paper derives Berends‑Giele recursion relations for higher‑derivative scalar QED and Yang‑Mills, confirming Ward identities and showing that massless gluon currents reduce to ordinary Yang‑Mills results. It also demonstrates that amplitudes involving massive Merlin modes vanish or match known results, suggesting future applications to higher‑derivative gravity and color‑kinematics duality.

papers.title: Fixed Points of the Yang-Mills Gradient Flow in the Vortex Sector
papers.abstract: We study the Yang-Mills gradient flow of center vortices in SU(2) gauge theory. For axially symmetric vortices the flow reduces exactly to a linear diffusion equation for the radial profile: a Gaussian core keeps its shape while its width grows as $\sqrt{R^2+4t}$, the flux is exactly conserved, and the thin vortex is the unique bounded fixed point, though not an attractor. Off-diagonal perturbations are governed by a pair of radial Schr\"odinger operators, and a variational computation shows that, frozen at any instant, the Abelian core has a tachyonic mode for every winding $n\geq 1$. Since the core spreads while the mode grows, we pass to self-similar variables, where the unstable modes are known in closed form, with growth exponents $\mu_{n,m}=n-1+m$. Multiply wound vortices are therefore unstable, while the fundamental vortex is exactly marginal and stays Abelian. A scaling argument rules out any static vortex in the transverse plane, and the instability acquires a simple geometric meaning that shortens the path traced in SU(2) by the holonomy of a growing loop, lowering the winding by two. The flow thus drives every vortex toward the Abelian core of winding $n \bmod 2$, with non-Abelian structure appearing only as the transient through which multiply wound cores unwind.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the Yang–Mills gradient flow for axially symmetric SU(2) center vortices, showing that the Abelian core evolves as a Gaussian diffusion and that multiply wound vortices possess tachyonic modes that drive them to unwind to a fundamental Abelian configuration. The study provides explicit self‑similar solutions and a geometric interpretation of the instability, but does not directly address holography, celestial amplitudes, or related algebraic structures.

papers.title: Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Courant-Hilbert Approach
papers.authors: Zahra Pezhman, Komeil Babaei Velni, H. Babaei-Aghbolagh
papers.abstract: It has been shown that for theories whose Courant-Hilbert function depends on a single dimensionful coupling, the energy-momentum tensor is controlled by the two combinations $\tau\dot{\ell}$ and $\ell-\tau\dot{\ell}$, so that the quadratic invariants $X=T_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}$ and $Y=(T^\mu{}_\mu)^2$ depend on a single auxiliary variable. Eliminating this variable in favour of $Y/X$ yields the exact autonomous flow $\partial_\lambda\mathcal L=X\,\mathcal F(Y/X)$, with no explicit dependence on the coupling, the electromagnetic invariants or the CH parameter, on every branch where the map is invertible. The expansion of $\mathcal F$ in powers of $\sqrt{Y/X}$ shows which flows are built from integer powers of $X$ and $Y$ and which require half-integer powers. In this paper, we work out four examples in closed form, each with its analytic structure and physical interpretation: the generalized Born-Infeld theory, whose flow is quadratic in the stress tensor; the $q$-deformed family, in which the odd coefficients of the expansion vanish at $q=1/2$ and are nonzero otherwise; the no-$\tau$-maximum theory; and the causal Russo-Townsend logarithmic theory, whose flow involves the lower real branch of the Lambert $W$ function and reproduces the known perturbative result. The singular points of $\mathcal{F}$ are related to the critical fields, energy conditions, and strong-field behavior of each theory.
papers.summary: This paper derives an exact autonomous flow for the Lagrangian of causal electrodynamics theories whose Courant-Hilbert function depends on a single dimensionful coupling, showing that the stress tensor invariants X and Y depend on a single auxiliary variable. It presents closed-form examples including generalized Born-Infeld, a q‑deformed family, a no‑τ maximum theory, and a causal Russo‑Townsend logarithmic theory, and discusses the relation of singularities in the flow to critical fields and energy conditions.

papers.title: Holographic entropy inequalities & typical states
papers.abstract: As a consequence of the Ryu-Takayanagi formula, static semiclassical states in AdS quantum gravity share a set of special properties expressible as linear inequalities on their entanglement entropies. How general are these properties? Do they still hold when we move away from the regime of validity of RT, i.e. static states in classical Einstein gravity? Do they perhaps hold even for some class of non-holographic states? We will motivate these questions and review what's known about the answers.
papers.summary: This paper reviews linear entropy inequalities derived from the Ryu–Takayanagi formula and investigates their validity beyond static semiclassical AdS states, including classical Einstein gravity and non-holographic settings. It discusses whether these holographic constraints persist in more general quantum gravity or field theory contexts.

papers.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories
papers.authors: Jiechao Feng, Nayan Myerson-Jain, G. Shankar, Taige Wang, Meng Cheng
papers.abstract: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.
papers.summary: The paper develops an analytical and numerical study of monodromy defects in O(N) conformal field theories, identifying stable defect CFTs via RG and large‑N techniques and confirming predictions with Monte Carlo simulations of the O(3) model. It highlights how defect boundary conditions control correlation functions and scaling dimensions in dimensions 3≤d<4.

papers.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons Model
papers.abstract: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $\kappa$. At large $|\kappa|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|\kappa|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Ho\v{r}ava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $\kappa$ drops below a critical value.
papers.summary: The paper studies a 2+1 dimensional nonrelativistic gravity theory with w∞ gauge symmetry, called unimodular Hořava‑Chern‑Simons gravity, and analyzes its renormalization group flow from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR Lifshitz fixed point with dynamical exponent z≈2−3/(2|κ|). It conjectures a phase transition to a confining phase when the Chern‑Simons level κ falls below a critical value.

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We establish global control of perturbative D-term data governing semiclassical vacuum sectors in chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. A closed-form, one-loop-exact D-term coefficient, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos (FI) parameters, gives a uniformly controlled leading potential away from massless thresholds and fixes local FI and Chern--Simons couplings near them. This allows lifting the 3d Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$ across the compact holonomy space. The framework is showcased by finding a remarkably rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple abelian model and reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory, first found on $S^3\times S^1$. The examples demonstrate the stakes of global matching: true vacua may lie at nontrivial holonomy even with nonzero threshold values of the Coulomb-slice D-coefficient, and despite vanishing D-coefficient at trivial holonomy.
papers.summary: This work derives a one‑loop exact expression for the D‑term potential governing semiclassical vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories compactified on (mathbb{R}^3	imes S^1). It applies the result to classify vacua in a simple abelian model and to reproduce the reduction of an (mathrm{SU}(2)) Maruyoshi–Song theory to the Gang–Yamazaki theory, illustrating how nontrivial holonomy can shift the true vacuum even when the D‑term vanishes at trivial holonomy.

papers.title: All-plus Yang--Mills and gravity wavefunctions in de Sitter space
papers.authors: Song He, Jiajie Mei, Yuyu Mo
papers.abstract: We present sewing representations for tree-level all-plus wavefunctions in four-dimensional de Sitter space. For Yang--Mills theory, the arbitrary-multiplicity formula is a sum over noncrossing polygon dissections, with each cell carrying energy differences of a full lower-point wavefunction. The absence of a generic total-energy pole is manifest, while partial-energy residues are determined by the lower-point factors. We derive this representation from self-dual Yang--Mills solutions. For Einstein gravity, we propose an arbitrary-multiplicity formula consisting of an alternating sum over labelled sewing trees plus a local gravitational Chern--Simons term. This local term arises from the self-dual Einstein action and supplies boundary data not fixed by internal-energy cuts. We derive a generating formula for it from the boundary connection and give explicit expressions through seven points.
papers.summary: The paper derives compact, self‑dual‑based sewing formulas for all‑plus tree‑level wavefunctions of Yang–Mills and gravity in four‑dimensional de Sitter space, revealing a non‑crossing polygonal structure for Yang–Mills and an alternating‑tree plus Chern–Simons term for gravity. These results provide explicit higher‑point expressions and clarify how boundary data are encoded in the wavefunctions, offering new tools for studying de Sitter holography and related scattering observables.

papers.title: Exact lattice bosonization of the double-scaled $c=1$ matrix model
papers.authors: Adwait Gaikwad, Gautam Mandal, Ajay Mohan
papers.abstract: In a recent paper by two of us, it has been shown that entanglement entropy (EE) of matrix quantum mechanics (or, equivalently, of a non-relativistic fermion model) has a natural interpretation in terms of an exact bosonization of the fermion theory in terms of a lattice boson with lattice spacing $\sim 1/N$ (where $N$ is the rank of the matrix, equal to the number of fermions). The theory of this lattice boson is distinct from a latticized version of the "collective variable'' theory which is formulated in terms of the fermion density $\rho(\lambda)$ ("collective variable''); it is, in fact, more closely related to the Wigner distribution of the fermions. In this paper, we develop this connection further for the $c=1$ double scaled matrix model. Even though $N$ becomes infinite, the double scaled theory is described by a boson on a finite and non-uniform lattice spacing, of order $\sim g_s(x) l_s$ (where $g_s(x) \equiv g_s {\rm cosech}^2(x/l_s)$ is a position dependent string coupling). We explicitly derive the $c=1$ EE, as well as the one and two-point functions of fermion density from the lattice boson. The results are explicitly finite, unlike the collective variable theory which is shown to yield divergent answers. Our results suggest that while local observables such as the EE and $\langle \rho(\lambda) \rangle$, are characterized by a unique short distance scale $g_s(x) l_s$, the asymptotic observables such as the S-matrix at every genus are characterized by a short distance scale $l_s$. We show how this arises and discuss a possible interpretation in terms of D0 brane physics.
papers.summary: This paper develops an exact lattice bosonization of the double-scaled (c=1) matrix model, deriving finite entanglement entropy and fermion density correlators from a non-uniform lattice boson tied to a position-dependent string coupling. It highlights a distinct short-distance scale for local observables versus asymptotic S-matrix data, suggesting a D0-brane interpretation within 2D string theory.

papers.title: Spiralling into Dark Energy: Axio-Dilaton Attractors in Light of Current Data
papers.abstract: In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-\xi\phi_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $\omega_\phi=(\lambda-2\xi)/(\lambda+2\xi)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $\xi\gg\lambda$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $\lambda\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}\xi\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $\Lambda$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539.
papers.summary: The paper studies the late‑time dynamics of an axio‑dilaton system with an exponential potential and a kinetic coupling to a massless axion, finding a non‑geodesic attractor that can drive accelerated expansion if the kinetic coupling dominates the slope. Bayesian fits to DESI, Pantheon, and Planck data constrain the slope λ to be ≳7–9 and the coupling ξ to be ≳10^2.5, slightly improving over ΛCDM but leaving polynomial corrections indistinguishable.

papers.title: Nonlinear Higher-Spin Theory in $O(4,1)$ de Sitter Space
papers.authors: O. A. Gelfond, M. A. Vasiliev
papers.abstract: Four versions of the higher-spin gauge theory compatible with $O(4,1)$ de Sitter geometry in presence of fermions are proposed. Two of them exhibit the structure of $\mathbb{Z}_2\times \mathbb{Z}_2$ Lie superalgebra proposed originally by one of the authors for the description of de Sitter supergravity \cite{Vasiliev:1985vtv}. Two of the proposed models are unitary in the bosonic sectors in analogy with the recent proposal by Lang and Neiman \cite{Lang:2026inn} and admit a pseudo involution in presence of fermions suggesting possible (anti)unitarity associated either with the time reversal in $dS_4$ or with the space-time doubling.
papers.summary: The paper constructs four distinct higher‑spin gauge theories on four‑dimensional de Sitter space that incorporate fermionic degrees of freedom. Two of these models realize a $mathbb{Z}_2	imesmathbb{Z}_2$ superalgebra and exhibit unitary bosonic sectors together with a pseudo‑involution that could encode time‑reversal or spacetime doubling in dS$_4$.

papers.title: Two-node Dualities from Elementary Dualities in 3d and 4d
papers.abstract: A new 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ two-node Seiberg-like duality, analogous to the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ Intriligator--Leigh--Strassler~(ILS) duality, is proposed. As strong evidence, we check the agreement between the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ ellipsoid partition functions for numerous cases using s-confinement method. Surprisingly, our derivation assumes only two elementary 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ dualities: Aharony and Benini--Benvenuti--Pasquetti, which reinforces the idea dualities from dualities. We also revisit the original ILS duality and provide a derivation based on nodewise dualities. In particular, we apply a sequence of Seiberg and Kutasov--Schwimmer dualities to individual gauge nodes, with Higgsing at an intermediate step, and subsequently integrate out the massive fields.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a new 3d N=2 two‑node Seiberg‑like duality analogous to the 4d N=1 Intriligator–Leigh–Strassler duality, deriving it from the elementary 3d dualities of Aharony and Benini–Benvenuti–Pasquetti and checking it with ellipsoid partition functions. It also gives a nodewise derivation of the original ILS duality using Seiberg and Kutasov–Schwimmer dualities with intermediate Higgsing and integrating out massive fields.

papers.title: Reparametrisation invariance, anomalies and pseudoscalar states in massless quantum electrodynamics
papers.authors: Joshua Cesca, Archil Kobakhidze, Elden Loomes
papers.abstract: In electrodynamics, and more generally in gauge theories, quantisation introduces an ambiguity whereby the vector current, the axial current, or both may acquire an anomalous divergence. These anomalies can be classified as relevant, conventionally associated with the infrared properties of the theory, and irrelevant, arising from the freedom in the choice of renormalisation scheme. We show that, under a axial reparametrisation of the fermion fields, the global axial symmetry can be promoted to a gauge redundancy. Requiring this gauge symmetry to be preserved at the quantum level eliminates the irrelevant anomalies, leaving a non-propagating pseudoscalar field that acts as a Lagrange multiplier enforcing the familiar axial anomaly. We further argue that, on topologically non-trivial spacetimes, in particular those with non-trivial second cohomology, this axial gauge symmetry can undergo a Higgs mechanism, rendering the pseudoscalar field an emergent propagating degree of freedom. Finally, we briefly point out an analogous emergent state associated with the conformal anomaly.
papers.summary: The paper shows that by promoting the global axial symmetry to a gauge redundancy via an axial reparametrisation, one can eliminate irrelevant anomalies and introduce a non‑propagating pseudoscalar that enforces the axial anomaly. On manifolds with non‑trivial second cohomology this pseudoscalar can acquire a mass through a Higgs‑like mechanism, turning it into an emergent propagating mode, with a brief discussion of a similar effect for the conformal anomaly.

papers.title: Graph-Based Algorithms for Worldline EFT Integrands
papers.abstract: We present novel graph-centered algorithms for the construction and representation of worldline effective field theory (WEFT) integrands that separate the topological and algebraic structure of loop integrands into independent graph-numerator pairs. In this representation, the graph encodes all propagators, worldline source and sink vertices, momentum routing, i0 prescriptions, and proper-time dependence, while the numerator carries only the minimal algebraic, tensorial content. To construct integrands at fixed post-Minkowskian order we propose a generalized Berends-Giele construction that minimizes the number of expensive tensor contraction operations. We also discuss simplification and canonicalization strategies through "serialization" of worldline propagators and the application of "selfie"-subdiagram partial-fraction identities, yielding a minimal canonical topology basis. We further show that the graph-numerator representation naturally generalizes the notion of an integral family and its sectors, relevant for integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction: propagators are not constrained to a single master labeling, and each sector carries its own minimal set of independent scalar products, completing into an overcomplete global family. This setup minimizes the total number of required integral sectors through an optimal use of sector symmetries and enables independent optimization of propagator labeling for IBP reductions. The algorithms are implemented in the Rust crate FeynRIR, which is currently able to efficiently compute integrands for the variation of the effective WEFT action, the equations of motion for the worldlines and the (radiation-reacted) impulse.
papers.summary: The authors develop graph-based algorithms to construct worldline EFT integrands, separating propagator topology from algebraic numerators and enabling efficient Berends‑Giele recursion and IBP reduction. These methods are implemented in Rust (FeynRIR) and streamline the computation of worldline actions, equations of motion, and radiation‑reacted impulses.

papers.title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy
papers.abstract: We explore effective field theory (EFT) realizations of the dark dimension (DD) scenario in which the size of the DD is determined by the competition between a 5D quintessence potential and the Casimir energy. When only contributions from massless fields are considered, the Casimir energy does not have a typical energy scale, and the 4D dark energy (DE) scale is set by the height of the 5D quintessence potential. The simple 5D model we first study has an attractive feature that the size of the DD is related to the 4D vacuum energy (VE), as outlined above. However, it turns out that the 4D VE thus obtained cannot work as the 4D DE in the standard cosmological setting. One of the discrepancies between the VE and the DE manifests in the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's gravitational constant. This leads us to explore a 5D model in which the 4D Einstein-Hilbert (EH) action is dominantly induced by quantum effects, leaving the radion dependence of the 4D Newton's constant subdominant. This model leads to an attractive cosmological model, realizing the mechanism explained in the beginning. We also explore a 6D model with the total internal volume fixed, to make the 4D Newton's constant independent of the radion. We first study a scenario in which the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions are of the same order. In this scenario, the physical origin of the size of the DD is left to its UV completion. Next, we turn to a scenario in which there is a large hierarchy between the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions. In this scenario, the energy scale of the 5D quintessence potential turns out to be much higher than the energy scale of the 4D DE as inferred from the cosmological observations, so we need to subtract a constant term in 4D to tune the 4D DE. This prevents us from obtaining the scaling relation for the DE expected in the dSDC.
papers.summary: The authors study a 5D quintessence potential competing with Casimir energy to fix the size of a dark extra dimension, and show that naive models fail to reproduce the observed dark energy due to radion‑dependent Newton’s constant. They then construct a 5D/6D setup where the 4D Einstein–Hilbert term is largely induced by quantum effects, yielding a consistent cosmology but requiring fine‑tuning of the 4D vacuum energy.

papers.title: Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Auxiliary Field Formalism
papers.authors: Zahra Pezhman, H. Babaei-Aghbolagh, Komeil Babaei Velni
papers.abstract: Causal self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics admits a simple auxiliary-field description: the Lagrangian is linear in the two Lorentz invariants of the field strength, and the dynamics is encoded in a potential $W(\varphi)$ of a single auxiliary variable. We study non-perturbative $T\bar T$-like flows of these theories in this formalism. The irrelevant (stress-tensor) deformation acts on the potential by a rescaling, while the marginal ModMax-type deformation translates its vacuum. We derive the resulting flow equations exactly, show that the irrelevant exact $T\bar T$-like flow takes the autonomous form $\partial_\lambda\mathcal L=X\,F(r)$, where the closed form kernel $F$ depends only on the ratio $r=-T^\mu{}_\mu/\sqrt{4X-Y}$ of stress-tensor invariants. We also give an explicit reconstruction of the auxiliary potential from a given kernel. Causality imposes the differential inequality $D(r)>1/(1-r)$, while a globally single-valued kernel requires the ratio $r$ to be monotonic along the auxiliary branch. We examine the relation between the evenness of the exact $T\bar T$-like flow , the $\varphi$-parity of the potential, and the analyticity of the Lagrangian in the electromagnetic invariants, including the effect of a marginal ModMax parameter. We construct the linear auxiliary and Hamiltonian formulations and show that the Hamiltonian flow is governed by the same exact $T\bar T$-like flow with the opposite sign. We also express Born's Legendre self-duality, the two characteristic cones, and the energy conditions in terms of the kernel. In particular, $r=(\varepsilon-p_\perp)/(\varepsilon+p_\perp)$ has a direct physical interpretation. Exact $T\bar T$-like flow s are obtained for generalized Born-Infeld, logarithmic, q-deformed, and no-$\tau$-maximum electrodynamics.
papers.summary: This paper develops an auxiliary-field formalism for causal self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics and derives exact non-perturbative T̄T-like flows that act as rescalings of the auxiliary potential. The authors analyze causality constraints, kernel reconstruction, and provide explicit flows for several well-known models, offering a framework that could inform holographic duals of deformed gauge theories.

papers.title: The one-loop QCD scale anomaly on ADE orbifolds as an index
papers.abstract: We derive the one-loop scale anomaly of $\SU(N)$ Yang--Mills on the orbifold $\R^4/\Gamma$, with $\Gamma\subset \SU(2)$ a finite subgroup, from an equivariant index theorem on twistor space. The anomaly separates into the QCD $\beta$-function and a contribution localized at the orbifold fixed point. This localized term inherits the gravitational Weyl anomaly of the smooth ALE resolution, which concentrates under the singular degeneration, along with an additional unprotected heat-kernel coefficient.
papers.summary: The paper computes the one-loop QCD scale anomaly for SU(N) Yang–Mills on ADE orbifolds R^4/Γ using an equivariant index theorem on twistor space, separating the result into the standard β‑function and a localized term at the orbifold fixed point that inherits the gravitational Weyl anomaly of the ALE resolution.

papers.title: On memory effects in odd spacetime dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of a new electromagnetic memory effect in all odd spacetime dimensions. This effect is a universal property of electromagnetic fields sourced by charged particles of constant momenta, appears at the Coulombic order and is directly related to the Weinberg soft theorem. We provide a unified derivation of this effect in all higher dimensions by evaluating the Maxwell constraint on a null plane at large, finite distance. We observe that in odd spacetime dimensions, the lightray integral computing the memory effect does not commute with the large-$r$ expansion. Our results necessarily assume that the lightray integral is taken prior to the $r \rightarrow \infty$ limit. The effect vanishes in the opposite order of limits, in agreement with previous results. We compute the Coulombic order electromagnetic memory effect for both massless and massive sources in all higher dimensions, explain its relation to the Fourier transform of the leading soft photon theorem and present a protocol for its measurement in a finite time parametrically larger than the distance of a detector from the sources. We conclude with comments on the generalization to gravity.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates a universal electromagnetic memory effect in all odd spacetime dimensions, arising from charged particles with constant momenta and appearing at Coulombic order. It connects this memory to the leading soft photon theorem and outlines a measurement protocol, offering insights that may inform celestial amplitude studies.

papers.title: Theory and Cosmology of Biverse Volume-Normalized Gravity
papers.abstract: This dissertation expounds the biverse volume-normalized gravity, a novel theoretical framework of classical and quantum gravity that provides an unusual solution to the cosmological constant problem, the 60-degree-of-magnitude discrepancy between the value of the vacuum energy density in our universe predicted by particle physics and that implied by cosmological data. In the literature, there exist two interesting ideas: 1) to use the "volume-normalized" action functional, the usual action of the particle Standard Model and general relativity but divided by the spacetime volume, first proposed by Tseytlin; 2) to generate the vacuum energy density dynamically by assigning a ghost-free massive potential to the graviton. However, each has a problem: Tseytlin's attempt suffers from diverging quantum loops and the massive gravity theory has a second metric tensor with questionable origin and the quantum strong coupling problem. Inspired by these two ideas, as well as the AdS/CFT correspondence in string theory, the biverse volume-normalized gravity extends Tseytlin's idea by placing our (3+1)-dimensional universe on the boundary of a (4+1)-dimensional bulk space. This new adaptation controls the large quantum gravity loops in the limit of vanishing ratio of the spacetime volume of our universe to that of the other universe. The ghost-free massive gravity can then be seamlessly incorporated, not only that its otherwise nebulous second metric tensor appears naturally as the pullback of the bulk metric on the boundary, but its strong coupling problem also solved. The biverse volume-normalized gravity is also consistent with all tested models of particle cosmology and the evolution of the universe, and nontrivially predicts that the tensor-to-scalar ratio of our universe is exactly zero.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a biverse volume‑normalized gravity framework that extends Tseytlin’s volume‑normalized action by embedding our 3+1D universe as the boundary of a 4+1D bulk, thereby taming quantum loop divergences and naturally incorporating a ghost‑free massive graviton. It claims consistency with standard cosmology and predicts a vanishing tensor‑to‑scalar ratio, offering a novel holographic route to the cosmological constant problem.

papers.title: The topological vertex is finitely generated
papers.abstract: The topological vertex computes all genus amplitudes for the open topological A-model in $\mathbb{C}^3$ with branes on three toric Lagrangians and, via gluing, both open and closed string amplitudes on any toric Calabi-Yau threefold. In this note we show that the topological vertex is generated by boundary interactions of three disks and three annuli. A generalization of this result is shown to hold for the refined topological vertex.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that the all-genus topological vertex for the A-model on C^3 can be built from a finite set of boundary interactions involving three disks and three annuli, and extends this finite generation to the refined vertex. This result simplifies the computation of open and closed amplitudes on any toric Calabi-Yau threefold by reducing the problem to a small set of elementary building blocks.

papers.title: Compositional Operational Rank, Smooth Realizability, and Dimensional Reduction
papers.authors: Nikolay D. Tulupov, Alexander M. Tishin
papers.abstract: Higher-dimensional theories distinguish the dimensionality of a microscopic description from the number of directions accessible to a physical observer. Relating these notions requires not only dimensional reduction, but also a consistent preservation of operational independence across different levels of description.   We establish sufficient conditions under which a compositional operational rank is preserved first as the dimension of a smooth integral leaf and then as an observable Fisher-information rank. The key requirement is closure-faithfulness: the smooth realization must preserve the dependency relations of the operational closure, rather than merely its total rank. Together with real representability, constant rank, involutivity, and observer/scale compatibility, this yields a local integral leaf whose dimension equals the operational rank.   A further primary-identification condition is required at the measurement level. If an independently specified observer image coincides locally with the primary integral distribution and the admissible protocols provide local resolution, finite labeled-mixture closure, and locally constant outcome support, then the same rank can be realized by a finite composite Fisher-information protocol.   The construction holds for arbitrary finite rank. At r = 4 it provides a conditional operational criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories: a viable reduction must preserve the relevant operational dependency structure, not merely produce four effective coordinates. Quantum-hardware negative controls further show that the same restricted Fisher rank can conceal different larger ranks under a broader pre-specified measurement protocol. The framework therefore constrains the operational outcome of dimensional reduction without imposing a universal four-dimensional bound on microscopic state spaces.
papers.summary: The paper develops a mathematical framework for preserving operational rank during dimensional reduction, introducing closure-faithfulness and smooth realizations to ensure that the dimensionality of a smooth integral leaf matches the operational rank. It provides conditions under which a finite composite Fisher-information protocol can realize this rank, offering a conditional criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories without imposing a universal four-dimensional bound.

papers.title: Quantum Field Theory on the Tangent Bundle
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum-field-theoretical framework on the tangent bundle in which gravitational and internal gauge structures are associated with different sectors of an affine tangent-fiber geometry. The translational sector supplies the coframe and its relation to teleparallel gravity. A reduced vertical spectral problem is based on the centrally extended Euclidean group \(E^{c}(2)\), motivated by projective representations of the stabilizer of a nonzero null vector. Twofold multiplicities of equivalent vertical representations in selected left-chiral sectors admit weak \(SU(2)\) actions, while an assumed threefold quark multiplicity admits a locally gauged color \(SU(3)_c\) symmetry. A proposed global quotient correlates the color center with vertical rotations on a threefold rotation cover. Together with the selected chiral spectrum and anomaly conditions, this construction reproduces the observed fractional quark charge assignments. We formulate matter and gauge-field quantization, BRST symmetry, and anomaly constraints. Under the stated projection assumptions, the color sector has the standard local QCD structure, including its one-loop beta function and asymptotic freedom. Additional gauge bosons and dark-matter states are proposed as hypothetical sectors. We also formulate a structural action for possible couplings between teleparallel torsion and additional Lorentz-sector potentials. The framework relates selected structures of particle physics and gravity within a common geometric setting; their further dynamical and phenomenological development remains open.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a QFT on the tangent bundle, linking teleparallel gravity with internal gauge symmetries via an affine tangent‑fiber geometry. It reproduces the Standard Model color sector and predicts additional gauge bosons and dark‑matter states, but does not address holography or scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: How to get an attractive model
papers.abstract: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.
papers.summary: The paper presents a previously overlooked fourth‑order Calabi‑Yau differential operator with a clear geometric interpretation, and shows it exhibits a rank‑two attractor structure. This suggests a new Calabi‑Yau threefold whose modularity mirrors that of an elliptic curve over ℚ, hinting at connections to l‑functions and Langlands‑type correspondences.

papers.title: Quantum Reversibility Meets Classical Reverse Diffusion
papers.authors: Ryota Nasu, Gota Tanaka, Asato Tsuchiya
papers.abstract: Bayes' rule connects forward and reverse processes in classical probability theory, and its quantum analogue has been discussed in terms of the Petz (transpose) map. For quantum dynamics governed by the Lindblad equation, the corresponding Petz map can also be written in Lindblad form. In classical stochastic systems, the analogue of the Lindblad equation is the Fokker-Planck equation, and applying Bayes' rule to it yields the reverse diffusion equation underlying modern diffusion-based generative models. It is known that a semiclassical approximation of the Lindblad equation yields the Fokker-Planck equation for the Wigner function, which is a quasiprobability distribution defined on phase space as the Wigner transform of the density operator. Here we demonstrate that applying the same approximation to the Lindblad equation associated with the Petz map produces an equation that coincides with that obtained from the Fokker-Planck equation via Bayes' rule. This finding establishes a direct correspondence between the Petz map and Bayes' rule, unifying quantum reversibility with classical reverse diffusion.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the quantum Petz map for Lindblad dynamics reduces, under a semiclassical approximation, to the same reverse diffusion equation obtained by applying Bayes' rule to the classical Fokker-Planck equation, thereby linking quantum reversibility with classical reverse diffusion. This establishes a direct correspondence between the Petz map and Bayes' rule, unifying quantum and classical notions of time reversal in stochastic processes.

papers.title: On the Energy Minimizing Problem in Plasma Dynamics
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in plasma physics and its applications to fusion theory is to find minimum energy stares of plasma.. Hong Qin has suggested the use of what he calls "Gromov ground states" which take into account the phenomenon of symplectic rigidity, as opposed to Gardner's classical approach which only use volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Howev4er Qin's approach leads to topological difficulties because his constructions remain in the classical (Hamiltonian) domain. We circumvent these difficulties by introducing a quantum-mechanical formulation of the problem, based on the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian state
papers.summary: This paper addresses the minimum-energy configurations of plasmas by introducing Gromov ground states that incorporate symplectic rigidity, contrasting with the classical volume-preserving diffeomorphism approach. It then extends the analysis into a quantum framework using the Wigner transform and Gaussian state symplectic geometry.

papers.title: A Low Scale for Quark-Lepton Unification
papers.authors: Lawrence J. Hall, Claudio Andrea Manzari, Clara Murgui
papers.abstract: The measured fermion masses may be pointing to the scale of quark-lepton unification. Studying the renormalization-group evolution of the Standard Model Yukawa couplings, we find that $y_\tau=y_b$ and $y_\mu=3y_s$ occur at nearly the same scale, around $10^6$ GeV, while the first generation reaches the Georgi-Jarlskog relation $y_e\simeq y_d/3$ at order $10^8$ GeV and can arise from the same Clebsch structure through a simple hierarchical flavor texture. This pattern naturally suggests low-scale Pati-Salam symmetry. We show that flavor mixing and finite threshold corrections preserve this picture. If the electron mass has an independent origin, the two heavier-generation relations can be realized in theories with a unification scale as low as $(5$-$7)\times10^5$ GeV. We identify two simple theories that accommodate all three relations and in which the measured masses fix the flavor structure. The first unifies all three generations at $4.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\times10^6$ GeV; the second, with symmetric Yukawa matrices, at $1.5^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times10^7$ GeV, and predicts $|V_{cb}|=0.042\pm0.002$. Their shared light-family texture fixes the relevant vector-leptoquark couplings, making $\mu\to e$ conversion in nuclei a direct test of unification: upcoming searches will probe part of the region selected by the two theories, and proposed facilities could cover it completely.
papers.summary: The authors analyze the renormalization‑group running of SM Yukawa couplings and find that several GUT‑inspired relations (yτ=yb, yμ=3ys, ye≈yd/3) emerge at a common scale of order 10^6–10^8 GeV, suggesting a low‑scale Pati‑Salam unification. They construct two minimal models that realize these relations, predict Vcb, and link the leptoquark couplings to observable μ→e conversion rates, offering a testable window into quark‑lepton unification.

papers.title: Direct tests of conformal symmetry with Rydberg atoms: assessment and proposals
papers.abstract: We propose a direct test of conformal symmetry using Rydberg-atom arrays. By arranging the atoms on a circle and measuring equal-time two-point correlation functions, the characteristic functional form predicted by conformal field theory can be tested directly. We estimate the number of experimental snapshots required to resolve this behavior with sufficient statistical precision. We further optimize the time-dependent ramp profile of the Rabi frequency~$\Omega$ and detuning~$\Delta$ used to prepare the target critical state adiabatically. The optimized profile achieves higher fidelity over much shorter evolution times than those employed in previous experiments. Taken together, these results suggest that a direct experimental test of conformal symmetry is feasible with current Rydberg-atom technology.
papers.summary: The authors propose a feasible experimental test of conformal symmetry using Rydberg‑atom arrays arranged on a circle, measuring equal‑time two‑point correlations to match CFT predictions. They also optimize the adiabatic ramp of Rabi frequency and detuning, achieving higher fidelity in shorter times, indicating that current technology can realize critical states for probing conformal invariance.

papers.title: A new analytical finding for the Born-Infeld integral potential
papers.authors: Leonardo Paulo Guimar\~aes De Assis, Priscila Vald\^enia dos Santos, Sergio de Oliveira Vellozo, Jos\'e Abdala Helay\"el Neto
papers.abstract: A new finding regarding the Born-Infeld potential for short range distances from the charge revealed that its integral form can be almost exact written as the difference between a Coulomb-type potential and a Yukawa-type potential. This allowed for an immediate physical interpretation in terms of classical vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Subsequently, a new U(r) is proposed to cover the entire space. This formulation is then applied to calculate, in a closed manner, the first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms; a comparison of these shifts with high-precision spectroscopic data provides a model-dependent lower bound for the maximum field intensity parameter b.
papers.summary: The paper presents an almost exact analytic representation of the Born‑Infeld potential as a difference between a Coulomb and a Yukawa term, enabling a clear physical picture of vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Using this form, the authors compute first‑order energy shifts in hydrogen‑like atoms and compare them to high‑precision spectroscopy to set a lower bound on the Born‑Infeld parameter b.

papers.title: Hitchin's $\alpha$-invariant and positive sectional curvature on homotopy $9$-spheres
papers.authors: Yang-Hui He, Ziran Liu, Shing-Tung Yau
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth homotopy $9$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature if and only if its Hitchin $\alpha$-invariant vanishes, or equivalently if and only if it admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.
papers.summary: This paper establishes a precise criterion for when a smooth homotopy 9‑sphere can support a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature: it is possible if and only if the Hitchin α‑invariant vanishes, which is equivalent to admitting a metric of positive scalar curvature. The result links a topological invariant to a geometric property, showing that the existence of such metrics is completely determined by a single algebraic invariant.

papers.title: Acoustic Schwarzschild-like black hole and analogous Hawking radiation in Einstein-bumblebee gravity
papers.authors: Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Yu Shi, Yuehua Xiao, Jiliang Jing
papers.abstract: We derive an acoustic Schwarzschild-like black hole and study its analogous Hawking radiation in Einstein-bumblebee theory by using Gross-Pitaevskii theory in the background of Schwarzschild-like spacetime. This black hole have two kinds of event horizons: one is the gravitational horizon $r_h=2M$(black hole horizon), the others are the internal and external acoustic horizons $2M<r_{ac-}\leq4M,\;r_{ac}\geq4M$(dumb hole horizon) which depend on the tuning parameter $\xi$ and Lorentz violation coupling constant $\ell$. The corresponding Hawking temperature $T_h$ depends only on $\ell$, however $T_{ac}$ depends on $\ell$ and $\xi$. The dumb hole temperature $T_{ac}$ has a maximum $T_{acm}=T_h/8$. When considering the scalar particles radiating from the dumb hole, we find that in low frequency, the grey-body factor increases with the tuning parameter $\xi$, but decreases with $\ell$. In the high frequency, it approaches to $1$. Its energy emission rate is similar to the Planck's black spectrum where there has a maximum at a given peak frequency $\omega_m$. The energy emission rate also increases with the tuning parameter $\xi$, but decreases with $\ell$. This opposite dependence relationship is the most experimentally valuable feature and can directly benchmark against observations of real astrophysical black holes.
papers.summary: This paper constructs an acoustic analogue of a Schwarzschild black hole in Einstein‑bumblebee gravity and studies its Hawking‑like radiation, finding that the acoustic horizon temperature depends on Lorentz‑violating parameters. The grey‑body factors and emission spectra show tunable dependence on the Lorentz‑violation coupling, offering a potential experimental probe of modified gravity.

papers.title: Krylov geometry and optimal recovery under uncertain coherent noise
papers.abstract: Recovery from a coherent rotation with an unobserved angle depends on both the encoding and what calibration reveals about the noise. We determine their combined limit for a known finite-dimensional generator and one final recovery. Two polynomial projections organize the answer. A physical Krylov chain separates correctable error amplitudes from their first state-dependent distortion; projection onto lower-angle powers identifies the part that a coherent decoder can cancel. Under explicit rank and moment conditions, their combination gives the exact leading optimal entanglement infidelity at weak noise and a recovery attaining it for any finite logical dimension. The optimal worst-input error lies between one and $d$ times that infidelity at leading order, for logical dimension $d$. When the angle distribution is unknown, we optimize one decoder for every distribution compatible with the calibration. When spectral and calibration frequencies are integer multiples of a common frequency, moment positivity turns this into an exact finite optimization. Small measured means can still allow rare finite rotations. If the sole calibration datum is $\beta_r=\mathbb E[\sin^{2r}(\theta/2)]$, with $\theta$ the wrapped rotation phase at that common frequency, the optimal worst-prior infidelity is $O(\beta_r)$ exactly when generator powers through degree $r-1$ are correctable. When the first uncorrectable power has degree $m<r$, the optimal loss scales as $\beta_r^{m/r}$, with a sharp coefficient fixed by a universal moment problem. In a loss-free four-photon memory, population measurements at two calibration durations retain the fully informed quartic error coefficient for a fixed symmetric narrow-noise family with positive variance and finite fourth moment; a single duration permits loss quadratic in the noise width.
papers.summary: This paper studies optimal recovery of quantum states subject to coherent rotation noise with unknown angle, using Krylov subspace techniques to characterize the leading-order entanglement infidelity and construct near-optimal decoders. It provides explicit formulas under moment and rank conditions, and discusses calibration strategies for finite-dimensional logical systems.

papers.title: Spectroscopy of the SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
papers.authors: Axel Maas, Sofie Martins, Georg Wieland
papers.abstract: We investigate the ground state spectrum of a dynamical scalar-fermion-gauge system with an SU(2) gauge group, a scalar doublet, and two degenerate generations of vectorial fermions under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect. To this end, we employ lattice methods using the HiRep code. We study the dependence of the system on the (bare) fermion mass and find that the spectrum remains unaffected, up to trivial fermion mass effects. The results are in line with a weakly coupled theory exhibiting the Fr\"ohlich-Morchio-Strocchi mechanism.
papers.summary: The authors study the spectrum of a dynamical SU(2) gauge theory with a scalar doublet and two generations of fermions using lattice simulations. They find that the ground state spectrum is essentially independent of the bare fermion mass, consistent with a weakly coupled theory exhibiting the Fröhlich-Morchio-Strocchi mechanism.

papers.title: Induced Bell-CHSH observables in the Fewster-Verch measurement scheme
papers.authors: M. S. Guimaraes, I. Roditi, S. P. Sorella
papers.abstract: The Summers-Werner theorem shows that the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory violates the Bell-CHSH inequality maximally on complementary wedges, but it is an existence statement: it exhibits neither the observables nor an apparatus that measures them. We give an explicit operator-level realization within the Fewster-Verch measurement framework, obtaining dichotomic Bell observables of a free Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions as observables induced by local couplings to Majorana probes. The induced system smearing factorizes exactly as $f_h=k\,b_{\lambda,h}$, so its support is controlled by the compactly supported coupling profile $k$; dichotomy is imposed by calibrating and normalizing the induced smearings rather than required of the probe observable; and a probe-only normal ordering yields the product of Alice's and Bob's induced bilinears, which the non-multiplicative induced map alone does not provide. Under explicit attainability hypotheses the induced observables saturate the Tsirelson bound in a state prepared from the vacuum. The construction extends to coupled scalar fields.
papers.summary: The paper constructs explicit Bell-CHSH observables for a free Majorana field in 1+1 dimensions using the Fewster–Verch measurement scheme, showing that the induced observables can saturate the Tsirelson bound in the vacuum state. It demonstrates how the induced smearing factorizes, how probe-only normal ordering yields the product of Alice’s and Bob’s bilinears, and extends the construction to coupled scalar fields.

papers.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics. It provides an exact solution of Einstein gravity and admits a finite completion. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. In this setup, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Pad\'e approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.
papers.summary: The paper investigates how a logarithmic deformation of the Reissner‑Nordström metric, sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, modifies the potential for a massive neutral scalar field, and computes its quasinormal and quasibound spectra using WKB, Leaver, and time‑domain methods. The authors find that increasing the scalar mass or the nonlinear coupling raises the barrier, weakens damping, and shortens lifetimes, while analytic approximations agree within a few percent.

papers.title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
papers.authors: M. Matushko, A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov
papers.abstract: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.
papers.summary: This paper constructs matrix representations of the BC_n associative Yang–Baxter algebra using Baxter–Belavin R-matrices and Komori–Hikami K-matrices, and applies them to build long-range spin-chain Hamiltonians via R-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero–Inozemtsev and Calogero–Moser systems. The resulting models include Haldane–Shastry and Polychronakos–Frahm chains with modified spin positions, offering new integrable structures in elliptic and trigonometric settings.

papers.title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
papers.abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $\theta$ and $\eta$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response.   By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $\theta$ and $\eta$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.
papers.summary: The paper studies how noncommutative phase‑space deformations affect an anisotropic oscillator and proposes an optomechanical protocol using Stokes‑like measurements to extract the noncommutativity parameters from the optical response. It derives the covariance matrix, Kerr phase, and an interferometric detection scheme to estimate θ and η experimentally.

papers.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
papers.abstract: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $\Lambda$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $\sigma$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(\sigma)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $a\Lambda\log(1/(a\Lambda))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(\Lambda,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(a\Lambda))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.
papers.summary: The paper studies the Fisher information metric on the space of lattice Gross‑Neveu actions with Wilson fermions in the large‑N limit, showing how the continuum limit behaves differently for long‑distance versus full‑field modes. It finds that irrelevant directions shrink at different rates, leading to a divergent curvature in the coupling plane and an infinitely distant critical point in Fisher distance.

papers.title: Exact spinning wormholes in five dimensions from Toda integrability
papers.abstract: We construct a new exact solution to the five-dimensional Einstein-phantom-scalar system that describes a rotating wormhole connecting two asymptotically flat regions. The solution represents a rotating generalization of the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole with equal angular momenta. Under the cohomogeneity-one ansatz, we demonstrate that the radial equations reduce to an integrable $A_1\oplus A_2$ Toda system, from which the general local solution can be obtained in closed form. This integrable structure enables us to implement the regularity and asymptotic-flatness conditions analytically, thereby singling out a three-parameter family of solutions characterized by the mass, the equal angular momenta, and the scalar charge. The resulting spacetimes are geodesically complete, horizonless and stably causal, and contain no curvature singularities. The Toda structure further allows us to prove the uniqueness of the wormhole throat and to derive a sharp upper bound on the angular momentum for a fixed throat area. We also establish the existence and uniqueness of an ergosurface with respect to the stationary frame that is nonrotating at one asymptotic end, while the opposite end rotates relative to this frame. In a suitable scaling limit, the scalar field vanishes and the solution approaches the exterior region of the extremal Myers-Perry black hole with equal angular momenta.
papers.summary: The authors present a new exact rotating wormhole solution in five-dimensional Einstein–phantom-scalar gravity, obtained by reducing the field equations to an integrable (A_1oplus A_2) Toda system and solving them in closed form. The resulting three-parameter family is horizonless, geodesically complete, and exhibits a unique ergosurface, with a scaling limit that reproduces the extremal Myers–Perry black hole.

papers.title: Fermion Mass and Mixing Patterns from Fusion Algebras
papers.authors: Jacques Distler, Can Kilic, Sanjay Mathai
papers.abstract: The large hierarchy of fermion masses in the Standard Model has long posed a challenge to be explained. One approach is to try to invoke a symmetry principle to dictate the structure ("texture") of the matrices of fermion Yukawa couplings to the Higgs field. Here we invoke noninvertible symmetries, specifically, fusion algebras, to provide such textures. In particular, the structure of the fusion-algebra can be used to assign labels to each field, which determines how suppressed any given composite operator is as a term in the Lagrangian. In UV completions, this can be interpreted as specifying a hierarchy of operators that in the IR effective theory become the Yukawa couplings to the Higgs field. Remaining agnostic of a specific UV model, we perform a Monte Carlo numerical scan over unknown Wilson coefficients, and we identify the rank-8 fusion algebra $\rm{FR}^{8,6}_8$ as the one providing the best fit for the textures of the up-quark, down-quark and charged-lepton Yukawa matrices. We also study the predictions for the CKM and PMNS mixing matrices, with the conclusion that none of the fusion algebras we study provide an accurate fit for the masses and mixing angles simultaneously. The fusion algebra structure ensures that the textures that we find are stable under RG running and persist down to low energies.
papers.summary: The paper explores how noninvertible fusion algebras can generate hierarchical fermion mass textures and uses a Monte Carlo scan to identify a rank‑8 algebra that best fits quark and lepton Yukawa matrices, while noting that none of the studied algebras simultaneously reproduce observed masses and mixings. It also discusses the stability of these textures under renormalization group evolution.

papers.title: Explaining the universal Hagedorn temperature in string models of hadrons with fixed endpoints or baryon junctions
papers.abstract: We derive the mass formulas and more accurate asymptotic expressions for the densities of states for string models of hadrons with one fixed heavy endpoint or a baryon junction. We show that strings with one fixed endpoint have the same Hagedorn temperature as ordinary open strings at the same tension and number of polarizations, despite the different Regge slopes of heavy-light and light mesons. This provides a microscopic explanation for the universality of the Hagedorn temperature recently found phenomenologically. We also find that the baryon-junction and quark-diquark pictures share this Hagedorn temperature and yield the same asymptotic mass dependence of the density of states, differing only by an overall normalization. The observed baryon mass spectrum provides little discrimination between the two pictures, although the baryon-junction model has a larger discrepancy with the observed Regge slopes.
papers.summary: The paper derives mass formulas and asymptotic densities of states for hadronic strings with a fixed heavy endpoint or baryon junction, showing that their Hagedorn temperature matches that of ordinary open strings. It also compares baryon-junction and quark-diquark models, finding identical asymptotic behavior but differing normalizations, with little empirical discrimination.

papers.title: $\Delta(1232)$ isobars and neutrino opacities in hot dense matter
papers.abstract:
We calculated the diffusion mean free paths of electron neutrinos and antineutrinos in hot, neutrino-trapped matter containing $\Delta(1232)$ isobars, as found in proto-neutron stars and neutron star merger remnants. We included charged-current absorption with the $N\Delta$ weak vertex of weak pion production, neutral-current scattering on all baryons and three-body antineutrino absorption on electron--baryon pairs, with relativistic mean-field kinematics. The reaction $ ar

At two to four times saturation density, where the reaction is open, it shortens the antineutrino mean free path from

Because antineutrinos are scarce at high lepton fraction, this changes lepton-number diffusion only at low lepton fraction, by up to \DtwoRedHi\% at these densities and by a factor of \DtwoRedLow\ at 1.5 times saturation density. For electron neutrinos, absorption on the $\Delta^-$ and, at low lepton fraction, the opening of nucleonic absorption shorten the mean free path by factors of up to
